page: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL cores running at 3.1 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 2400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 54132.74 and a PassMark CPU score of 44078.3. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1055.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1284.68. Memory performance is strong for large-block read-only bandwidth at 189.99 GB/sec, while small-block cached reads and large-block writes fall into the average range. The CPU's extended instructions test shows strong performance, supported by hardware flags such as AVX and AVX-512.

The instance offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads, databases, and multi-threaded applications. The inclusion of 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides high-speed local data access without requiring external network-attached storage, enhancing cost efficiency for disk-heavy operations. However, single-threaded tasks and LLM text generation represent notable performance bottlenecks, with LLM text generation for a small 135M model scoring in the bottom 10%. This instance is best utilized for multi-threaded processing, database operations, and static web serving rather than single-core intensive tasks or real-time LLM text generation.
